agentCan: Implement the authorization-code flow with rotating refresh-token persistence
Configure the app via settings UI or manifest; prepare values and listing content
Prepare the Marketplace submission packet (policy, design, security guidelines)

approval.cost: No submission fee stated in the docs read
approval.trigger: No review before real users can connect: an unlisted app can be installed by other teams via your authorization/install link. Marketplace listing is optional and traction-gated: you must first be a Miro Partner (Partner Interest Form unlocks the submission form), have the app on a public host, and meet BOTH thresholds: more than 50 Monthly Active Users in each of the last two consecutive months, and more than 10 installs on unique organizations. Review itself runs through a Jira ticket with the Miro Platform team as assignee and you as Reporter.
approval.wait: Marketplace review 'may take up to 8-12 weeks' (stated), after the traction thresholds are met

blockers.detail: At app creation you choose 'Expire user authorization token' or not, and 'you cannot enable, disable, or update this setting after you create your app'. Picking non-expiring tokens for convenience means recreating the app to get refresh-token security later.
blockers.howToClear: Choose expiring tokens at creation (Miro's recommended option) unless you have a specific reason not to.
blockers.title: The token-expiry choice is a one-way door

blockers.detail: Refreshing issues a NEW access token and a NEW refresh token, and 'the previous access token and refresh token become invalid'. A client that fails to persist the replacement pair atomically strands the connection.
blockers.howToClear: Persist both tokens in one atomic write on every refresh.
blockers.title: Refresh rotation invalidates the old pair

blockers.detail: Unlike review-only stores, you cannot submit on day one: the >50 MAU for two consecutive months plus >10 unique-org installs criteria force a pre-listing distribution phase via install links before Miro will even review you.
blockers.howToClear: Plan distribution via install URL first; treat listing as a later milestone and instrument MAU/installs from launch.
blockers.title: Marketplace eligibility is traction, not paperwork

alternatives: Non-expiring tokens (the access token remains valid until the user uninstalls the app from their team; chosen at creation, immutable)
'Install app and get OAuth token' in app settings (mints a token for your own Dev team without implementing any flow; the internal/service pattern)
Instant apps (Web SDK apps discovered in the board toolbar, permissions granted on first Run; a different consent surface)
flavor.recommended: An app in your Developer team with expiring tokens enabled (Miro's recommended option), standard authorization-code flow
flavor.why: Every app gets a Client ID and Client secret and a permissions set (boards:read, boards:write, identity:read). With expiring tokens, the code flow yields a 1-hour access token plus a 60-day refresh token. Marketplace is not a different app type: it is the same app after traction thresholds and review.

humanMust: Accept terms and create a Developer team
Create the app and make the irreversible expiry choice
Become a Miro Partner and run the Marketplace submission when eligible
name: Miro
nuances: Installation is per team: the token response carries the team_id the user installed into, and a non-expiring token dies when the user uninstalls your app FROM THEIR TEAM. Multi-team users mean multi-install bookkeeping.
Authorization codes expire 10 minutes after issue and are single-use.

Redirect URI matching is exact: the troubleshooting guide calls out even a www. prefix or trailing slash difference as a 4XX 'Redirect URI mismatch', and the token call's redirect_uri must match the authorize call's.
Auth endpoints stay on v1 (api.miro.com/v1/oauth/token) while the data API is v2; the docs explicitly note the auth endpoints are not deprecated.
On Enterprise plans, app creation/installation sits with Team Admins, and deleting a Developer team invalidates its apps' tokens: customer admins control whether your app can be installed at all.
prerequisites: A Miro account and a Developer team
App URL and OAuth redirect URI

steps.detail: Profile settings > Your apps: accept the terms and create a Developer team if you don't have one. Apps are owned by the Dev team.
steps.title: Create a Developer team

steps.detail: + Create new app: name it, select the Dev team, and decide the 'Expire user authorization token' checkbox NOW (it cannot be changed later). Recommended: expiring tokens. Click Create app.
steps.title: Create the app (make the expiry decision)

steps.detail: Note the Client ID and Client secret; set the App URL and OAuth redirect URI; select Permissions (scopes) in the settings UI or via the app manifest.
steps.title: Configure credentials, redirect URI, permissions

steps.detail: Send the user to miro.com/oauth/authorize (response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state, team_id). The user lands on an 'Install & authorize' page and picks/approves the team install. The code expires in 10 minutes and is single-use.
steps.title: Send the user to Install & authorize

steps.detail: POST to api.miro.com/v1/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code, and the exact same redirect_uri. Store the access token, refresh token, scope, user_id, and team_id ('You are responsible for storing and securing this token data'). Call the REST API v2 with Authorization: Bearer.
steps.title: Exchange the code; store the token set

steps.detail: Share the app/install URL directly (unlisted works immediately), or, once you are a Miro Partner with >50 MAU in each of the last two months and >10 unique-org installs, submit to the Marketplace. Review runs via a Jira ticket and 'may take up to 8-12 weeks'; a privacy policy link is mandatory in the listing.
steps.time: Submission ~30 min; review up to 8-12 weeks (stated)
steps.title: Distribute (link now, Marketplace later)

tagline: Conventional OAuth whose only hard gate is traction: anyone can install via your link today, but the Marketplace won't even review you until you show 50+ monthly users for two straight months and 10+ organization installs, then takes up to 8-12 weeks.

time.active: ~20 min of app configuration + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day for link distribution; Marketplace adds a traction phase plus up to 8-12 weeks of review
